prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: moving home mid-policy. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When the member has moved home mid-policy, I should treat the address change as a possible trigger for both cover and risk changes, then check whether the old and new properties overlap on the policy dates before I assess the loss."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the loss happened at the former address after the move date, I should not assume cover carries on automatically; I need to confirm the policyholder still had an insurable interest there and whether any occupancy or notification conditions were breached."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member says they were in the middle of moving, I should separate the timeline into pre-move, transit, and post-move periods, because contents, buildings, and accidental damage questions often turn on exactly where the item was at the time."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the new home is occupied before the policy change is logged, I should check for underinsurance or rating differences straight away, because the rebuild value, occupancy type, and security details may differ from what we held."},{"type":"preference","content":"When documents are unclear, I prefer to ask for the completion date, keys collected date, and actual move-in date, because those three dates usually resolve most mid-policy home move disputes without unnecessary back-and-forth."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a forwarding address is the only contact route after the move, I should not rely on post sent to the old address, and I should make one more attempt to reach the member before deciding the file is unresponsive."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a motor claim is linked to a move, I should check whether the vehicle was kept overnight at the new address, on-street, or in storage, because garaging and security can affect both cover and delegated authority decisions."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member reports damage during removals, I should ask whether a professional removals firm was used and whether the loss was from packing, handling, or transit, since the responsible party and recovery options may sit outside our first response."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the old property is left empty after the move, I prefer to flag the empty-home period immediately, because unoccupied-home conditions are often time-limited and can be decisive for escape of water, theft, and storm claims."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the member has moved because of a chain delay or temporary arrangement, I should avoid assuming a single fixed address for the whole claim, and instead map the insured risk to each address the member actually used during the period in question."}]}
